review_scope: Full 79-line pinned UI article read. Included fragments remain separate dependencies; no full-artifact accounting, rendered-version certification, rights clearance, or native test is asserted.

claims.statement: The UI protection claim is limited to supported secrets when creating, editing, or uploading files; it is not universal secret recognition.
The web UI displays one detected secret at a time; the displayed count is not the total detection denominator.
A secret already detected in the repository with an existing alert is not blocked again under the described behavior.
Organization owners can supply a custom blocked-push guidance link; linked vault, escalation, and history-rewrite examples do not authorize those operations.
The documented resolution removes the secret from the file before retrying the commit; a successful retry alone is not complete repository remediation evidence.
Bypass may require a reason; the author's belief that a secret is safe is not independent verification of that belief.
The bypass procedure calls for reviewing the detected secret's name and location before allowing it.
A missing bypass option is described as tighter administrator or owner controls, not a permission error that should automatically be repaired.
Delegated bypass requests go to designated reviewers for approval or denial; submitting a request does not grant permission.
Bypass requests expire after seven days; this statement does not establish the expiry of an already approved same-secret exception.
Approval permits the current changes containing the secret.
Approval also permits future changes containing the same secret, so it must not be represented as a one-commit exception.
After denial, the documented path is removing the secret before committing, not treating the denied request as an attestation.
